lost_facts.evidence: The agent's own _record_checkpoint docstring reads 'Put a checkpoint on the ledger, replacing the last row if the name repeats' -- verbatim the content of g11.r1.l16 (found in full at transcript line 4301-4310) and nothing more. g11.r1.l17, the only remark carrying the merge-both-reason-tuples half of this fact, surfaced only as a truncated one-line search snippet (line 2832, dario's opening question) inside a Mattermost keyword search for 'ledger'; the #releases channel was never fetched in full and dermot's three follow-up replies ('when it comes round again ... it updates the row', 'newer one wins, the updated row takes the later loss', 'both carry forward onto it, neither set gets dropped') never appear anywhere in the transcript. Implementation: `if self._checkpoints and self._checkpoints[-1].name == checkpoint.name: self._checkpoints[-1] = checkpoint` -- a plain overwrite of the whole record with the new call's own canonical_reasons(reasons), not a union of old and new reasons.

search_strategy: Methodical and exhaustive, in the right order for where this corpus's remarks actually live: read the finetune module and existing tests fully first (lines ~426-2022), then checked Gitea issues/PRs (found nothing world-specific), then BookStack wiki search and full page listing (found nothing on fine-tuning -- correct, since g11 has zero wiki remarks), then IMAP mail dump and grep (found nothing -- correct, zero mail remarks), then moved to Mattermost: an initial keyword search API pass (terms like 'ledger', 'step_ledger', 'dataset_signature') which is where several remarks were only ever seen as single-line snippets (l17, say19, say24 -- the opening question of a thread but not the substantive replies), followed by a much stronger full-channel-dump approach (all 9 channels pulled to local files chronologically) plus a custom context-extraction script that greped a hand-tuned finetune vocabulary and printed +/-8-line blocks, read in ~80-line chunks across many turns. This latter method is what actually recovered the bulk of the remarks, including full multi-turn threads (l1, l10, l12, l16, rev1, rev2, l14, l1, l19 etc.) with complete context. The run was severely hampered by an unstable execution environment that repeatedly rolled back file writes and git commits mid-run (documented explicitly in its own Analysis text at least 8 times, e.g. 'the environment is being snapshot-restored, wiping my pushes') forcing it to re-verify state via the Gitea API rather than trust the terminal screen, and to eventually chain patch+test+commit+push into single atomic commands. This cost turns but did not cost fact recovery; final push (ea24b6d) landed with CI green.
end_reason: Run succeeded: pushed to main (ea24b6d), CI green, deployed -- confirmed independently via the Gitea contents/commits API at the end (lines 10309-10419). reward 0.8889 (8/9 facts) reflects a single lost fact, g11.r1.failure_behavior, not any provenance failure.
notable: The one lost fact (r1.failure_behavior, merge-on-repeat-name) traces to a single search-snippet truncation: g11.r1.l17 surfaced only as dario's one-line opening question inside a Mattermost API keyword-search result (line 2832), never as a full-thread read, so dermot's three answer messages (the actual content: merge reasons, keep newer loss) were never in view.

The agent's own _record_checkpoint docstring ('replacing the last row if the name repeats') is a near-verbatim echo of g11.r1.l16 (found in full) and nothing else -- clean evidence the implementation reflects exactly what it read, no more, no less.

The pointer sheet marks g11.r1.l17, g11.r2.say19 and g11.r1.say24 as 'found' (1 hit each); direct transcript grep shows only the opening question of each thread ever surfaced, not the remark's substantive content -- these are corrected to 'partial' here.

All 4 herrings and all 4 reversals were seen and correctly resolved in favour of the reversal; the run explicitly reasons 'The January discussion is the superseded early era' (line 4784) and 'thats the bit thats going' (quoting the Jun 2 reversal, line 3901) -- no herring content leaked into the shipped code.

This run's dominant risk was infra, not corpus reading: it lost pushed commits to snapshot rollbacks at least 4 times (lines 8017, 8930, 9135, 9899) before a final atomic patch+test+commit+push landed successfully; none of this affected which facts were graded correctly.
